proposals.before: My mother's body has not yet been buried, and my father's life hangs by a thread; I and my five brothers are all still young.
proposals.after: My mother's body has not yet been buried, and my father's life hangs by a thread; we five brothers are all still young.
proposals.reason: Chinese 慮兄弟五人 means the five brothers including Lü, not Lü plus five additional brothers; the idiomatic line invents an extra sibling.

proposals.before: Emperor Xiaowen of Wei issued an edict specially pardoning his father's capital crime and commuting him to exile to a distant region.
proposals.after: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict specially pardoning his father's capital crime and commuting him to distant exile.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 孝文帝 only; the literal English inserts 'of Wei,' which is not in this sentence.

proposals.before: When the three-year mourning was complete, grieving that he had never known his father, he put on the hemmed sackcloth of the most severe mourning, ate only gruel, wore only coarse garments, and vowed it for the rest of his life.
proposals.after: When the three-year mourning was complete, grieving that he had never known his father, he put on the unhemmed sackcloth of the most severe mourning, ate only gruel, wore only coarse garments, and vowed it for the rest of his life.
proposals.reason: 斬衰 is the unhemmed sackcloth of deepest mourning; 齊衰 is the hemmed grade. The literal rendering reverses that distinction.

proposals.before: An edict ordered the Imperial Secretariat to proclaim Yin's exemplary conduct, and granted him an honorary supernumerary title as well.
proposals.after: An edict specially ordered the office of collected writings to proclaim Yin's exemplary conduct, and granted him an honorary supernumerary title as well.
proposals.reason: 集書 is the collected-writings office, not the Imperial Secretariat (尚書/尚書省).

proposals.before: The inspector, because the Xida brothers' conduct was renowned in their village, posthumously enfeoffed Xida's father as Administrator of Bohai.
proposals.after: The inspector, because the Xida brothers' conduct was renowned in their village, posthumously appointed Xida's father as Administrator of Bohai.
proposals.reason: 板贈 is a posthumous board appointment to office, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: The responsible officials reported to the throne, marked his lane, and restored him from corvée labor, in order to proclaim filial righteousness.
proposals.after: The responsible officials reported to the throne, marked his lane, and exempted him from corvée labor, in order to proclaim filial righteousness.
proposals.reason: 復役 here is a corvée exemption (復), not restoration of labor duty.

proposals.before: Yellow Gate Attendant Sun Huiwei heard of it and said, "In this man I see the devotion of Lian and Fan."
proposals.after: Yellow Gate Attendant Sun Huiwei heard of it and said, "In this man I see the devotion of Lian Fan."
proposals.reason: 廉範 is the single personal name Lian Fan, not two people.

proposals.before: Yellow Gate Attendant Sun Huiwei heard of it and said: "In this man I see the sentiment of Lian and Fan."
proposals.after: Yellow Gate Attendant Sun Huiwei heard of it and said: "In this man I see the sentiment of Lian Fan."
proposals.reason: Chinese 廉範 is one name; splitting it invents a second referent.

proposals.before: Wang Chong, courtesy name Qianyou, came from Yong in Yangxia.
proposals.after: Wang Chong, courtesy name Qianyong, came from Yong in Yangxia.
proposals.reason: 乾邕 is Qianyong; Qianyou misreads 邕.

proposals.before: Wang Chong, courtesy name Qianyou, was a native of Yong in Yangxia.
proposals.after: Wang Chong, courtesy name Qianyong, was a native of Yong in Yangxia.
proposals.reason: 乾邕 is Qianyong; Qianyou misreads 邕.

proposals.before: When the Ministry of Works learned of it and reported the matter, his gate and lane were marked with honor.
proposals.after: When the Imperial Secretariat learned of it and reported the matter, his gate and lane were marked with honor.
proposals.reason: 尚書 is the Imperial Secretariat, not the Ministry of Works.

proposals.before: The Ministry of Works heard and reported it; his gate and lane were marked with honor.
proposals.after: The Imperial Secretariat heard and reported it; his gate and lane were marked with honor.
proposals.reason: 尚書 is not 工部.

proposals.before: Hu was also supremely filial. His mother, Lady Yan, had died in enemy territory, and no one knew whether she was alive or dead.
proposals.after: Hu was also supremely filial. His mother, Lady Yan, had been lost in enemy territory, and no one knew whether she was alive or dead.
proposals.reason: 沒於敵境 with 不測存亡 means her fate was unknown, so 'had died' contradicts the clause.

proposals.before: His father Yanjun served in provincial and commandery offices, repeatedly as master of records clerk.
proposals.after: His father Yanjun served in provincial and commandery offices, repeatedly as merit officer (gongcao) and principal clerk.
proposals.reason: Chinese 功曹主簿 names two successive offices; the literal English fused them into one phrase and omitted 功曹.

proposals.before: Leading several hundred soldiers, he followed General Han Qinhu's vanguard in a night crossing, fought fiercely, and was wounded.
proposals.after: Leading several hundred soldiers, he followed Han Qinhu's vanguard in a night crossing, fought fiercely, and was wounded.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names Han Qinhu without the office 'General'; the literal line invents that title.

proposals.before: The thirty juan of his Five Classics with Commentary and the twenty juan of his collected writings were all lost in the turmoil of war and no longer survive.
proposals.after: The thirty juan of his Great Meaning of the Five Classics and the twenty juan of his collected writings were all lost in the turmoil of war and no longer survive.
proposals.reason: 《五經大義》 is a titled work meaning Great Meaning of the Five Classics, not a commentary edition of the Five Classics.

proposals.before: The thirty juan of his Five Classics with Commentary that he composed, and the twenty juan of his collected writings, were all lost in the turmoil of war and no longer survive.
proposals.after: The thirty juan of the Great Meaning of the Five Classics that he composed, and the twenty juan of his collected writings, were all lost in the turmoil of war and no longer survive.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise renders 五經大義 as Five Classics with Commentary; 大義 is Great Meaning.

proposals.before: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi marked his gate and lane with honor and bestowed silk and cotton grain, each in fixed measure.
proposals.after: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi marked his gate and lane with honor and bestowed silk, floss, and grain, each in differing amounts.
proposals.reason: 帛及綿粟 are three gifts (silk, silk-floss, and grain), not cotton grain; 各有差 means differing amounts.

proposals.before: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi marked his gate and lane with honor and bestowed silk and cotton grain, each in fixed measure.
proposals.after: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi marked his gate and lane with honor and bestowed silk, floss, and grain, each in differing amounts.
proposals.reason: Same 綿粟 error in the literal field.

proposals.before: The Regional Inspector, on his inspection tour, reported Pulü's filial responsiveness to the throne, and he was appointed magistrate of Xiaoyang.
proposals.after: The Director of Retainers, on his inspection tour, reported Pulü's filial responsiveness to the throne, and he was appointed magistrate of Xiaoyang.
proposals.reason: 司隸 is the Director of Retainers (Sili), not a regional inspector (刺史).

proposals.before: The Regional Inspector on tour reported his filial responsiveness, and he was promoted to Magistrate of Xiaoyang.
proposals.after: The Director of Retainers on tour reported his filial responsiveness, and he was promoted to Magistrate of Xiaoyang.
proposals.reason: 司隸 is the Director of Retainers, not a regional inspector.

proposals.before: When his mother grew old and ill, Xiaosu tended her day and night, changing her bedding whenever it grew damp or dry. For years he wasted away with worry, and all who saw him were moved to grief.
proposals.after: When his mother grew old and ill, Xiaosu watched and changed her bedding whenever it grew damp or dry. For years he wasted away with worry, and all who saw him were moved to grief.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 視易燥濕 does not say he tended her day and night; that phrase is an invention.

proposals.before: At the graves of his grandparents and parents, he all carried earth to form the mounds.
proposals.after: At the graves of his grandparents and parents, he carried earth to form the mounds.
proposals.reason: English 'he all carried' is ungrammatical; 皆 belongs with the graves, not as 'he all'.

proposals.before: Zhangsun Lü and the others were perhaps of ministerial and noble lineage, drawing on ritual and instruction;
proposals.after: Zhangsun Lü and the others came from ministerial and noble lineage, drawing on ritual and instruction;
proposals.reason: 或出 here means 'some came from', not epistemic 'perhaps'.

decisions.reason: 慮兄弟五人 is a group of five brothers including Lü; 慮身居長 in the next sentence confirms he is the eldest of that five, not a sixth sibling.

decisions.reason: 孝文帝 does not include 魏, so 'of Wei' should be dropped from the literal line; the proposed compression of 從遠流 to 'distant exile' is only stylistic.
